goals.title: The sea keeps what fits
goals.critique: This is round 7's candidate again (the eighth version of the sea-builds-land line), and the only new parts are a GPU surf strip as the first step and stripes from three sands; the pitch is still a run-on paragraph, and 'hand-building loses to the sea' is still an untested tuning claim. The storm wave that leaves a longer striped tongue behind three stones is a strong picture, and dig, place, then watch the next wave answer is a well-judged loop. But after eight rounds not one wave has been filmed next to one stone, and re-pitching adds nothing until that first step exists.

goals.title: Burrows in the hill
goals.critique: It sits closest to the human's direction: digging scoop by scoop, gathered sticks that carry load by where they are set, a hill that keeps every tunnel, and a trickle from the roof as a warning you read at once; a buried friend dug out to a cheer is a clip people send. But digging through sand that caves in is familiar from falling-sand and mining games, so anything memorable has to come from moisture and shoring, and the pitch never says how a player reads load in a stick. The friends' room wishes are one line each with no rules behind them, and a hill-scale granular solver with moisture and stick loads is two hard unbuilt systems, so the damp-versus-dry film has to come first.
